sentences.text: South Australia’s Independent Commissioner Against Corruption reviewed the operation and effectiveness of the Whistleblowers Protection Act 1993 at the Attorney-General’s request.
sentences.support:
The Attorney-General has requested me to conduct that review and report to 
him.

sentences.text: The review considered protected disclosures, reporting pathways, confidentiality, victimisation remedies and oversight within the state’s integrity framework.
sentences.support:
That WBL include an offence for disclosing the identity 
of a person who has made a public interest disclosure

sentences.text: The Commissioner concluded that the Act should be replaced because it was not fulfilling its purpose of encouraging disclosures and protecting those who made them.
sentences.section: WBP Act – Amendment or Repeal and Re-enactment?
sentences.support:
I do 
not think it is fulfilling its primary objective of facilitating disclosure and 
providing protections for those who make disclosures.

sentences.text: The Commissioner made 30 recommendations addressing replacement legislation, investigation duties, reporting channels, whistleblower protection and oversight.
sentences.support:
That WBL provide an obligation, subject to appropriate 
exceptions, to investigate disclosures.

findings.quote:
The WBP Act be repealed and a new Act be 
substituted that clearly addresses the four fundamental issues relevant to 
whistleblowing and the further recommendations mentioned in this review.

notes: There is no executive summary or equivalent synopsis; a List of Recommendations appears on PDF pages 8–12. The summary draws on the Commissioner’s assessment and recommendations, not submissions or findings from research cited within the review.
